method.title: How we read NL-48
method.intro: NL-48 is an insurer’s public disclosure of health-service turnaround times. We transcribe cashless pre-authorisation and discharge buckets by TPA and individual/group policies. These are insurer-reported figures, not a patient survey or an independent compliance audit.
method.bucket: The 2–6 hour bucket spans the three-hour discharge deadline. We do not estimate the share decided before or after three hours.
method.clock: The disclosure clock starts when the TPA receives the discharge bill. Family-entered submission times may capture a different point.
method.rows: Rows with different TPAs, periods, policy types or units are not combined. Published percentages retain their rounding.
method.sample: A sample size is shown only when the exact cashless denominator is identifiable. A missing denominator is not zero.
method.coverage: Missing, scanned, malformed and inconsistent filings are tracked explicitly. Coverage remains incomplete; comparisons are not a compliance ranking.
method.patients: Patient reports are voluntary and unverified. Published groups require at least ten reports. Small groups, individual timestamps and hospital names are not displayed.
method.auditBody: Each row records source URL, PDF page, insurer, TPA, period, unit and retrieval date. The repository contains the reproducible transcription pipeline, source hashes, exclusions and spot-check evidence.
method.correctionsBody: Open a source-linked issue in the public repository. Do not include policy numbers, medical records or personal details. Contact verification means a detail appeared on an official source; it does not mean a call was made or an inbox tested.

privacy.continuityBody: Cases stay in this browser. You can switch cases, delete one case, or attach confirmed deduction lines to it. A backup contains the selected timeline and attached lines, never the original document. Backup files are not encrypted: keep them private. Import shows a preview and asks before replacing the selected case.
privacy.transfer: Encrypted transfer: ciphertext only, 7 days, no identity.
privacy.transferBody: If you choose to transfer a case, your browser encrypts it before sending it. ClaimClock stores only the encrypted bytes, a hashed lookup code, expiry time and lookup count. The private key travels in your transfer text or the QR link fragment and is removed from the address bar before verification loads. It is never sent to our server. Keep the full transfer text private: anyone with it can read the case. The short lookup code alone cannot decrypt it.
privacy.transferRetention: Transfers stop working after 7 days or 3 successful ciphertext lookups, whichever comes first. A lookup counts even if the entered private key is wrong. The third lookup deletes the stored ciphertext; expired rows are removed by hourly cleanup. A failed cleanup may delay physical deletion, but cannot extend access. Each encrypted transfer is limited to 64 KB. We cannot recover a lost key.
privacy.turnstileBody: Optional reports, AI explanations and transfer creation or lookup use Cloudflare Turnstile in invisible mode. It loads only when you choose one of these actions and processes connection and browser signals to check for abuse. ClaimClock does not send document text, case details or the private transfer key to Turnstile. The app adds no login or cookies; any Turnstile cookies are governed by Cloudflare. Existing shared quotas still apply.

reimb.title: Cashless denied? Collect these 7 papers before leaving the hospital
reimb.intro: A cashless denial is not a final claim rejection. It only means the insurer did not approve direct payment to the hospital right now. You can pay, collect these original documents before leaving, and file a reimbursement claim.
reimb.item1: 1. Written cashless denial / query note and the cashless reference number
reimb.item2: 2. Final itemised hospital bill and numbered payment receipts reconciling any deposit
reimb.item3: 3. Final discharge summary signed and stamped
reimb.item4: 4. Certified Indoor Case Papers (ICP), daily doctor notes, vital/IV charts and OT notes
reimb.item5: 5. Treating doctor’s signed note explaining why inpatient admission was clinically necessary
reimb.item6: 6. All original lab/imaging reports, prescriptions and pharmacy invoices
reimb.item7: 7. Implant / stent / lens invoice and original barcode sticker (if any device was used)
reimb.button: Prepare request to hospital desk for these papers
multi.title: Using two policies (Corporate + Personal)?
multi.intro: If one policy (such as an office group policy) covers only part of your hospital bill, you can claim the remaining admissible balance from your second policy.
multi.step1: Get the Claim Settlement Letter from the first insurer/TPA showing total bill, paid amount and unpaid balance.
multi.step2: Before leaving the hospital, take hospital-attested (stamped) copies of the final itemised bill, discharge summary and reports (since the first insurer keeps originals).
multi.step3: Submit the balance claim to the second insurer and ask both insurers to coordinate under Chapter I paragraph 18(a).

privacy.accountBody: My Vault works without any account. If you create one, you sign in with a passkey (no password, phone number or email). Your vault — name, family members, policies and attached cases — is encrypted in your browser with a key that never leaves your devices; the server stores the encrypted copy, your passkey’s public key, a random account id and a hashed session token. We cannot read the vault or recover its key. Deleting the account removes all of these at once. Sessions expire after 30 days.

compare.title: Compare plans on what matters at the hospital
compare.lead: Not premiums — the clauses that cut a claim: room rent, co-payment, waiting periods, consumables, the check-up benefit, and how fast each insurer actually clears cashless discharge in its own IRDAI disclosures.
compare.caution: ClaimClock sells nothing and earns nothing from any insurer. Every cell links to the insurer’s own document and the date we read it; “not verified” means exactly that. This is published-rule comparison, not a recommendation to buy.

advice.separateSeniors: {seniors} member(s) are 60 or older alongside younger members. A floater is priced on the eldest ({eldest}), and senior-specific terms (co-payments, shorter PED waits) differ: consider a separate policy for the seniors and a floater for the rest.
advice.seniorCopay: Entry at 61 or above triggers a mandatory co-payment in several plans (10–30% in this catalogue). Compare the co-payment row before the premium.
advice.seniorPedWait: For a senior, the pre-existing disease wait matters most: it ranges from 12 to 36 months across this catalogue, and ported years count towards it.
advice.declarePed: {count} member(s) have a diagnosed condition: declare every condition in the proposal. Non-disclosure is the leading reason for repudiation; after 60 months of continuous cover it can no longer be used against a claim.
advice.topUp: For four or more members, a base policy plus a super top-up (one aggregate deductible a year) usually gives a larger cover than a single large base policy — check whether the top-up’s deductible is per claim or per year.
advice.floaterEldest: Everyone is under 60: a family floater priced on the eldest member ({eldest}) is the usual structure; one claim draws down the shared sum insured, so size it for the costliest likely admission.
advice.childNeedsAdult: Children are covered as dependants on an adult’s policy; most retail plans need at least one adult proposer.
advice.roomRent: Prefer “any room” or a category rule over a 1%-of-sum-insured cap: a capped room triggers proportionate cuts on surgeon, OT and consultant charges — the most common deduction we see.
advice.consumables: Check whether consumables (gloves, syringes, kits) are covered in the plan, by a rider, or not at all — the second most common deduction.
advice.moratorium: Keep the first policy alive and renew on time: the 60-month moratorium and every waiting period count from continuous cover, and a lapse beyond the grace period restarts them.
advice.notRecommendation: This is structural guidance from published rules, not a recommendation of any insurer or plan. ClaimClock earns nothing from policy sales.

voice.consentIntro: Talk to ClaimClock hands-free, in English or Hindi. Before the microphone is turned on, here is exactly what leaves this device:
voice.consentAudio: Your voice: each thing you say (up to 25 seconds) goes through our Cloudflare Worker to a speech model, is turned into text and is not kept.
voice.consentText: That text, plus a summary of your saved policies — plan, sum insured, dates, and who is covered by relation and age; never names, policy numbers, UHIDs or claim numbers — goes to a language model so it can pick which ClaimClock tool to run. The current providers are named on the privacy page.
voice.consentNothingStored: ClaimClock stores nothing from the conversation. It lives in this window and is cleared when you close it. Tools run on this device with your saved data.
voice.consentAdvisory: Answers are information, not legal advice. Every figure comes from a cited rule or a number you gave; when a rule is not verified, the assistant says so.

privacy.voiceBody: The voice assistant is optional and asks for consent before the microphone is turned on. While it listens, each thing you say (up to 25 seconds) is sent through our Cloudflare Worker to the speech model named in the dialog and turned into text; the audio is not kept. That text, with a summary of your saved policies (plan, sum insured, dates, and who is covered by relation and age — never names, policy numbers, UHIDs, claim numbers, phone numbers or email addresses, which the Worker also strips by pattern) goes to the language model named in the dialog. The model only chooses which ClaimClock tool to run; the tools run on this device with your saved data, and letters it drafts never go back to the model.
privacy.voiceBody2: ClaimClock keeps no audio or server-side log of a conversation. Your chats with Saathi are saved on this device only (like your cases), so you can reopen or continue them; they are never synced or sent anywhere, and you can delete any chat from the Chats list. Spoken answers use your browser’s own voices, or an optional premium voice when the operator has enabled one (named below). Each request is checked by Cloudflare Turnstile and counted against a shared budget, so Saathi can be busy at times. Answers are information, not legal advice, and every figure comes from a cited rule or a number you gave.

renewal.lead: Your dates, what really changed in the premium, how to port or migrate without losing the credits you earned, and the 30-day free look when a new policy is not what was promised. Everything runs on this device; nothing is sent anywhere.

renewal.rule.renewal-not-denied-for-clai: A health policy is renewable unless the product is withdrawn or there was established fraud, non-disclosure or misrepresentation. The insurer cannot refuse renewal because you claimed, and cannot ask for medical tests or a fresh proposal form at renewal unless you raise the sum insured.
renewal.rule.renewal-loading-portfolio-o: For an individual policy, a renewal premium increase must apply to the whole product (the portfolio), not to you because you claimed. An insurer may give you a discount for a good claim record, but not a claim-based loading.
renewal.rule.senior-premium-cap-10pct: For indemnity-based individual health policies held by senior citizens (aged 60 and above), insurers may not revise premium rates by more than 10% a year; a larger revision, or withdrawing such a product, requires prior consultation with IRDAI. The direction took effect on 30 January 2025.
renewal.rule.grace-period-15-30-days: If you miss the renewal date you still have 15 days (monthly premium) or 30 days (quarterly, half-yearly or annual premium) to pay. Renew inside that window and every credit — sum insured, no-claim bonus, waiting periods served, moratorium months — is protected. Unless you pay in instalments, there is no cover for the days between the due date and the late payment.
renewal.rule.gst-exempt-individual-healt: From 22 September 2025 there is no GST on individual health policies, including family floaters and senior-citizen plans; group and employer policies still carry 18%. Removing 18% GST lowers an unchanged bill by about 15.25%, so compare the premium before tax to see the real change.
renewal.porting.compareHint: 60 to 30 days before renewal. Use the catalogue comparison for room rent, co-pay, consumables and waiting periods.
renewal.porting.applyHint: For the entire policy and every family member on it. Inside 30 days the new insurer may still accept you until 15 days before renewal, but need not.
renewal.porting.discloseHint: A fresh proposal form means fresh disclosure; an omission can be used against a claim later.
renewal.porting.recordsHint: The new insurer asks through the IIB portal; your current insurer must answer within 72 hours of that request.
renewal.porting.decisionHint: Counted from receipt of your records. The deadline is for the decision, not a guarantee of acceptance.
renewal.porting.creditsHint: Sum insured, no-claim bonus, waiting periods served and moratorium months carry over up to the previous limits — get them written on the new schedule.
renewal.porting.keepOldHint: If the new policy is not issued by the due date, renew the old one; the grace period protects credits but can leave a gap in cover.
renewal.migration.whenHint: For all family members on the policy. The insurer may accept a later request but need not; no charge for migration.
renewal.migration.creditsHint: Sum insured, bonus, waiting periods served and moratorium months move with you; a richer product may add waits for the extra benefits only.
renewal.migration.decisionHint: From receipt of the proposal or of the last document asked for (Citizens’ Charter for health insurance).
renewal.migration.groupExitHint: At exit, or when the group policy is modified or withdrawn; subject to underwriting, with the credits you built up.
renewal.migration.renewalRightHint: Nor may the insurer demand medical tests or a new proposal form at renewal unless you raise the sum insured.

tracker.title: Paid the hospital yourself? Make the 15 days count.
tracker.lead: A reimbursement claim must be settled within 15 days of submission, and a late one earns interest the insurer has to add on its own. Track the clock, log every document query, keep the seven papers together, audit the settlement, and check the bill against CGHS reference rates. Everything stays on this device.
tracker.caution: Dates and interest here are computed from the rules cited below and the dates you enter; the insurer’s acknowledgements are the record. CGHS rates are a public reference for asking questions, not a cap on what a private hospital may charge.

tracker.fairBillTitle: Is this bill line far above the public reference?
tracker.fairBillBody: The Central Government Health Scheme publishes package rates for 2,000 services, by city tier and hospital type. Match a bill line to a CGHS item and see the reference range for your city. Lines far above it are the ones to ask about — with the hospital’s own displayed rate card in hand.

voice.card.reimbursementRule: Reimbursement claims are settled within 15 days of submission; a late settlement earns Bank Rate + 2% from intimation, paid suo-moto.
tracker.rule.reimbursement-15-days: A reimbursement (non-cashless) health claim must be settled within 15 days of the day you submit it. Keep the dated acknowledgement of submission; the 15 days are counted from it.
tracker.rule.penal-interest-bank-rate-pl: If the insurer misses the settlement deadline, you are entitled to interest at the RBI Bank Rate plus 2% a year, counted from the day the claim was intimated to the day it is paid — and the insurer must add it on its own, without a demand. Check the settlement letter for the interest line.
tracker.rule.documents-at-one-go: The insurer must list every document it needs in one go, as specified in the policy document, instead of asking for one paper at a time. A second or third query for documents is itself a grievance — and it does not restart the settlement clock.
tracker.rule.claim-not-closed-for-docume: The insurer cannot reject or “close” your claim because a document is missing or because you intimated the claim late. It can only ask for the document — once, at one go — and must decide the claim on its merits.
tracker.rule.rate-display-rule-9: In the states and union territories that have adopted the Clinical Establishments Act, every hospital must display the rates it charges for each service, in the local language and English, where patients can see them. You may ask for that rate card and for the package break-up of your bill. The ranges of rates that Rule 9(ii) refers to have not been notified, so the CGHS rates on this page are a reference, not a cap.
